office_does: The county clerk keeps Kitsap County Superior Court records and filings, helps judges, lawyers and the public through the court process, and handles jury administration and passport services.
race_blurb: Two candidates who prefer the Democratic Party: incumbent David T Lewis III, a 41-year veteran of the office and clerk since 2021, faces deputy clerk Brien Kennedy, a former tech and e-commerce executive who promises a public audit, plain-language guides and monthly office hours. This is the third contested clerk race in 28 years.

candidates.summary: Kitsap County Clerk since 2021 after more than four decades in the clerk's office; president of the Washington Association of County Clerks.
highlights: Appointed clerk in 2021, elected in 2022; 41+ years in the clerk's office [S1]
Cites e-filing as a modernization that improves access to justice [S1]
Endorsed by the Kitsap County Democrats and the 26th LD Democrats [S1]

experience.basis: Four decades in the office and the sitting clerk since 2021; president of the state clerks' association.

candidates.summary: Deputy clerk for about a year and former Amazon, Microsoft and e-commerce executive, running a first campaign on accountability and plain-language public service.
highlights: Pledges a full public operational audit of the clerk's office [S3][S1]
Promises plain-language guides, monthly public office hours and an annual report, with no added staff or budget [S3][S2]
Says 'Unopposed races must stop'; this is the third contested clerk race in 28 years [S2][S1]
Has been in the clerk's office just over a year after a private-sector career [S4]

experience.basis: First-time candidate who argues repeatedly for fresh eyes and outside management experience over long tenure in the office.

spending.basis: Proposes a public audit of contracts, staffing and technology spending and improvements 'without more staff or more budget'; does not call for cuts.
